## Measured: the release lane's 43-minute median is 96% one step, then doubled by serialisation

All figures read from the jobs' own `started_at`/`completed_at`, not from an assumed clock. Sample: the last 30 `Changeset Release` runs (2026-08-19T14:35Z → 2026-08-20T09:58Z), 20 of them successful.

### Where release time actually goes

| | successful runs (n=20) |
|---|---|
| median | **43.3 min** |
| mean | 47.1 min |
| min / max | 30.1 / **70.9** min |

Step breakdown of run [32350122326](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32350122326) (the 70.9-min one):

| step | elapsed |
|---|---|
| Set up → Checkout → Corepack → Node → Turbo cache → **Install** | **33 s total** (install itself 7 s) |
| **Run tests** | **34 min 04 s** |
| Build packages | 35 s |
| Create Release PR / Publish to npm | 12 s |

**Caching is not the problem — `pnpm install` takes 7 seconds.** Effectively the entire job is `Run tests`.

### Cause 1 — the release job runs the test suite unsharded

`changeset-release.yml` calls `pnpm test`, and root `package.json` has `"test": "vitest run"` — the whole suite, one runner.

`ci.yml` shards the same suite 4 ways, and its own comment states the trade deliberately:

> That cost shards near-linearly, and the fixed overhead of an extra runner here is only ~30s … so 4 shards cut wall clock ~3x for ~26% more runner minutes.

Measured both ways on the same commit `9f118b934`: sharded on the PR, the whole CI run was **9 min 47 s** wall clock (slowest shard 9 min 43 s). Unsharded in release: **34 min**. Ratio 3.5x — consistent with the comment's ~3x.

### Cause 2 — releases serialise, so the wait is added on top

`concurrency: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with **no `cancel-in-progress`**, so the default applies and runs queue rather than cancel.

The handoff is exact, not inferred:

- run `32349908848` created 08:39:35, ran 38.0 min → finished **09:17:35**
- run `32350122326` created **08:42:12**, but its *job* was created **09:17:35** and started 09:17:37

So that run waited **35 min 23 s** before starting, then executed 35 min 27 s. The 70.9 min total is **half pure queueing**. The same pattern repeats at 04:51:35 / 04:51:52 (35.1 min then 69.1 min).

With roughly 18 merges to `main` in a working day and ~35 min of execution each, this lane is close to permanently saturated, so each merge inherits the backlog of the ones before it.

⚠️ **The obvious fix is the wrong one here.** ⛔ Do not add `cancel-in-progress: true` to a workflow whose last step is `changeset publish` — that cancels a release mid-publish. The lever is to stop spending 34 of the 35 minutes on tests: shard them, or drop the test step from the release job on the grounds that the same commit was already tested on its PR (see the caveat below, which weakens that second option).

---

## Three findings the measurement turned up alongside — filed here, not acted on

These are reported, not fixed; two of them are safety issues rather than speed issues.

### 1. ⚠️ The merge queue runs no CI at all

`CI` runs with `event=merge_group`: **total_count = 0** — with and without a `status` filter.

Counter-probed, because a zero is not a reading: the identical call with `event=push` returns 30 runs, and `event=pull_request` resolves normally (run `32354059728` reports `"event":"pull_request"`). The method works; the zero is real.

Independently corroborated: **PR #5334 was enqueued at 09:41:26Z and merged at 09:41:43Z — 17 seconds.** No CI run completes in 17 seconds.

This is the precise hole `ci.yml`'s own comment block was written to close (#3523), including its account of 2026-08-07, when #3503/#3510/#3516 merged with `Type Check` at `conclusion=failure`. The comment says the `merge_group` trigger is subscribed; the run count says it has never produced a build. **Whatever the mechanism, the queue is currently a rubber stamp and PR-level checks are the only real gate** — which is also why "the commit was already tested on its PR" is a weaker argument than it looks.

### 2. ⚠️ CI has not run on `push`/`main` since 2026-08-07

Newest `CI` run with `event=push`, `branch=main`: **2026-08-07T23:55:27Z**, ~13 days ago.

Pushes to `main` clearly still happen — `Changeset Release` has 3901 runs, the newest today at 09:58Z. So this is not "pushes stopped". The push lane is where `test-coverage` lives (`if: github.event_name == 'push'`, unsharded, `timeout-minutes: 40`), so **Codecov has had no report for ~13 days**, and the job whose 40-minute budget was sized for the push lane is not running.

### 3. `release.yml` is dead

The workflow named **"Release"** (`release.yml`, id 223155593) has **0 runs**. It triggers on `push: tags: v*`, and nothing pushes those tags. Counter-probed by the same method that returns 3901 runs for `Changeset Release`.

Worth knowing when reading this issue's title: "release" in practice means `changeset-release.yml`, not `release.yml`.

---

⛔ No changes made — the seat is paused at the maintainer's instruction; this is measurement only. Findings 1 and 2 look like they want their own cards, but I have not filed them pending a word, and filing would need the usual duplicate search first.

## Correction to finding 2 above, and the optimisation plan it changes

### ⚠️ Finding 2 in my previous comment was wrong

I wrote that CI had not run on `push`/`main` since 2026-08-07. **That is false.** I took it from a filtered query (`branch=main` + `event=push` + `status=completed`) whose newest result was Aug 7, and I did not counter-probe it against the unfiltered set — the same discipline I applied to the `merge_group` zero two paragraphs earlier, and skipped here.

Unfiltered, the most recent 30 CI runs contain 13 `push` runs on `main`, the newest **today at 09:58:23Z**. Codecov is not 13 days stale. I apologise for the noise.

The correction makes the real picture **worse**, not better, which is why it matters.

### What actually happens on every merge to `main`

| lane | what runs | measured |
|---|---|---|
| PR | 4 test shards, no coverage | **~9 min 47 s** ✅ |
| merge queue | nothing (`merge_group` runs = 0) | 17 s ⚠️ |
| push → **CI** | `Test (coverage)` — **unsharded**, v8 instrumentation; the 4 shards are `skipped` here by `if: github.event_name != 'push'` | **~39 min** |
| push → **Changeset Release** | `pnpm test` — **unsharded** | **~34 min** (+ up to ~35 min queued) |

So the full suite runs **twice per merge, unsharded, in parallel** — roughly 73 minutes of runner time — and neither run gates anything: the CI push run is cancelled by the next merge (`cancel-in-progress: true` keyed on `github.ref`), and the release run only delays publishing something already on `main`.

Job breakdown of the 09:58:23Z push run ([32356587040](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32356587040)):

| job | elapsed |
|---|---|
| **Test (coverage)** | **39 min 26 s** — ❌ failure |
| Type Check | 8 min 57 s |
| Build Docs | 4 min 53 s |
| Build & E2E | 59 s |
| Changeset Fixed Group Check | 6 s |
| Test (shard …/4) | skipped |

### ⚠️ `Test (coverage)` is 34 seconds away from its own timeout

That job has `timeout-minutes: 40` and just ran **39 min 26 s**. Whatever else is decided, this one is urgent on its own: the next natural growth in the suite turns it into a timeout, and a timeout renders as a red that has nothing to do with the commit.

### ⚠️ `main` is currently red, and the release caused it

The failing step is a real assertion, not the timeout:

```
scripts/__tests__/quick-reference-current-release-4143.test.ts:444
expected []   received [ "17.5.0" ]
```

A test pinned to "the current release" went red once `changeset version` wrote 17.5.0 into the tree. A PR cannot catch this, because the version bump happens *after* merge. Pinning the expected value instead of reading it from the manifest guarantees one red `main` per release.

---

## Proposed optimisation — ⛔ NOT actioned, this is on the manual floor

Every item below either removes a test step, lowers how often a gate runs, or raises a timeout. That is **门禁削弱**, which the standing rules put squarely on the maintainer: *"AI 有把 CI 弄绿的结构性动机, 削弱农场必须是人的动作"*. So this is a proposal for a ruling, not a plan I intend to execute.

**1. Drop `pnpm test` from `changeset-release.yml`** — biggest win, lowest risk.
Release goes from ~35 min to **~2 min** (install 7 s + build 35 s + publish 12 s), and the queueing disappears with it, because the lane stops being occupied for 35 minutes at a time. What that step tests is a commit **already on `main`** — failing it does not keep anything out, it only blocks publishing after the fact. Crucially this is removing the *second* post-merge full run, not the only one: the CI push lane still runs the whole suite.

**2. Fix `Test (coverage)`.** Raise `timeout-minutes` past 40 immediately regardless of what else is chosen. Then either shard it 4 ways and merge the blob reports (the workflow comment declines this on merge-cost grounds — that trade was priced before the job sat at 39 minutes), or stop running coverage on every push and run it daily / post-release, since Codecov is a trend signal and does not need every merge.

**3. Make the merge queue actually check something** — correctness, not speed.
`merge_group: types: [checks_requested]` **is** subscribed in `ci.yml`, yet `merge_group` runs = 0. GitHub only dispatches `checks_requested` when the queue has required checks configured, so the empty set is in the **repository ruleset**, not the YAML — ⛔ this is a settings change, not a PR. Doing this also strengthens item 1: once the queue validates before merge, a post-merge test run in the release job is even less load-bearing.

**4. Un-pin the release-coupled test** so a release stops turning `main` red — read the current version from the manifest rather than asserting a literal.

⚠️ Do **not** "fix" the release queueing with `cancel-in-progress: true`: that workflow's last step is `changeset publish`, and cancelling it mid-publish is worse than waiting.

Rough saving if 1 + 2 are taken: ~34 min of runner time per merge (~10 h/day at ~18 merges), and release latency from a 43-min median (71 min worst case) down to a couple of minutes.

## Independent re-measurement is in (#5395) — three of my numbers were wrong, and one conclusion reverses

The verification card came back. Full evidence is on #5395; this is what changes **here**, including corrections to my own earlier comments on this issue.

### ⚠️ Correction 1 — my retraction's stated *cause* was itself unverified

Above, I retracted the false "CI hasn't run on push/main since Aug 7" finding and blamed a **stale filtered query**. The re-measurement could not reproduce that: the same filter combination returns the correct newest run through **both** raw REST and the MCP wrapper, and no single `status` term reproduces the Aug-7 result.

So the false finding was real, but **the explanation I gave for it is not established**. I should have said "I don't know why that query returned Aug 7" instead of supplying a mechanism that sounded right. That is the same failure mode as the "path-based short-circuit" I invented earlier in this session — inventing a cause is not the same as finding one.

### ⚠️ Correction 2 — the release lane does not queue, it **drops**

I claimed `concurrency` without `cancel-in-progress` serialises releases and that a run can wait ~35 min. **The mechanism is confirmed but the magnitude is refuted**, and the real behaviour is worse in a different way:

- median release wait: **5 min 08 s**, not ~35 min
- waiting is **22%** of release wall clock, not half
- **95 of 200 release runs never executed at all** — with `cancel-in-progress` unset, GitHub holds only one pending run per group and **discards** the rest, rather than queueing them

That reframes the fix. The concern is not merely latency: **release runs are being thrown away**, and the one-run-per-group pending slot means merges land without their release run ever starting.

### ⚠️ Correction 3 — merge volume

I estimated ~18 merges/day. Measured median is **49 pushes to `main`/day** (only 2 of 400 are the changesets bot's own commit). My per-day saving figures are therefore **~2.7× too low**.

### Confirmed, and one of them understated

- **Full suite twice per merge, unsharded** — confirmed.
- **The 40-minute cap is not a future risk. It has already fired 4 times**, with GitHub's own annotation: *"The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 40m0s."* I filed this as "34 seconds of margin"; it has been over the line repeatedly.
- **Cancellation** — confirmed.
- Durations confirmed as magnitudes, though each figure sits at a different point of a moving distribution.

### Sharded coverage, priced

| | measured |
|---|---|
| unsharded | **39 min 05 s** |
| 4-way sharded | **12 min 04 s** (3.24×) |
| extra runner minutes | **+9.2%** |
| the blob-report merge `ci.yml` declines on cost grounds | **13 seconds** |

Equivalence checked rather than assumed: 1287 files both ways, 55432 vs 55395 of 84590 statements, `onlyUnsharded=0`, `onlyMerged=0`, delta **−0.0437 pp** — against a noise floor of 3 statements between two identical sharded runs.

**The stated reason for not sharding costs 13 seconds and buys back 27 minutes.**

### ⚠️ The finding that outranks this whole issue — #5402

`Test (coverage)` has failed **100% of the time since 2026-08-16T12:48Z**: `scripts/__tests__/check-package-self-import.test.ts` times out at 15000 ms **under v8 coverage instrumentation**. An ablation isolates coverage, not sharding, as the discriminator — 0 occurrences in 220 PR-lane runs (sharded, no coverage), 50 of 51 completed push-lane failures (unsharded, with coverage).

**Codecov has received nothing for four days**, for two independent reasons: the upload step is skipped by its implicit `success()`, and the live unsharded recipe leaves no `coverage/` directory at all when the suite fails.

⚠️ **This corrects my ACCEPT on #5394.** I wrote there that `main`'s red was cleared. It is not: PR #5396 removed the release-drift failure, which was real and recurring, but `Test (coverage)` was already failing for this independent reason and still is. The push run for that merge (`fd227eae1`) was itself **cancelled**, so it never returned a verdict at all — the newest *completed* verdict on `main` remains `failure`. I should have verified a green before saying so.

### Where that leaves the proposal

The ordering changes. **#5402 comes first** — the push lane has been reporting nothing but red for four days, so "the CI push lane still runs the whole suite" (my stated safety argument for dropping the release job's tests) has been false the entire time. Sharding is now cheap and well-evidenced. The queueing item should be rewritten around dropped runs rather than latency. All of it still needs a maintainer ruling; ⛔ nothing has been changed.

## Maintainer ruling — 2026-08-20: all recommendations accepted

Maintainer, 2026-08-20, in chat with the `repo:objectui` execution seat (session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`). Verbatim: **「接受你的所有建议，现在开始处理。」**

This clears the **门禁削弱 manual floor** for the specific items below and nothing else. Each item's scope is what is written here; anything discovered mid-implementation that goes beyond it returns to the maintainer under the roll-back clause rather than being decided by a seat.

### Ruled, in execution order

The order is load-bearing, not a preference. Items 2 and 3 remove or replace validation, and the safety argument for each depends on the item before it actually working.

| # | item | state |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Fix `Test (coverage)`** — `check-package-self-import.test.ts` times out at 15000 ms under v8 coverage; failing 100% since 2026-08-16, Codecov dark 4 days | **#5402**, first, blocks the rest |
| **2** | **Shard `Test (coverage)` 4 ways** (39m05s → 12m04s, +9.2% runner, 13 s blob merge) **and fix the upload's implicit `success()`** — both live in the same `test-coverage` job | new card, `Blocked-by:` #5402 |
| **3** | **Remove `pnpm test` from `changeset-release.yml`**, and **stop concurrency dropping runs** (95 of 200 never executed) — same file, one card. ⛔ **Not** `cancel-in-progress: true`: the last step is `changeset publish` | new card, `Blocked-by:` item 2 |
| **4** | **Delete `release.yml`** — 0 runs, ever; tag-triggered on `v*` which nothing pushes | new card, independent |
| **5** | **Fix `assertCanonicalVitestInvocation`** — does not cover the 17 packages carrying their own `vitest.config.ts`, contrary to its own docstring | new card, independent |

⚠️ **Why 3 comes last, and why my original ordering was wrong.** I first proposed removing the release job's tests as the top item, arguing the CI push lane still ran the whole suite as a backstop. Item 1 proves that backstop **has been red 100% of the time since 2026-08-16**. Removing release-side tests before 1 and 2 land would leave `main` with no working post-merge validation at all.

### ⛔ Not actionable by any seat — still the maintainer's, in repository settings

**The merge queue runs no CI** (#4986, `type:Bug`, on `pm:on-hold` since 2026-08-17; re-verified today: `merge_group` runs = 0, and PR #5334 went enqueued → merged in **17 seconds**). `ci.yml` already subscribes `merge_group: types: [checks_requested]`; GitHub only dispatches that event when the queue has **required checks** configured, so the empty set is in the repository ruleset. ⛔ **No PR can close #4986.** Until it is configured, the PR lane is the only validation any change to `main` receives — which is also the standing premise `AGENTS.md` §9 relies on and which has never been true.

The related **#5397** (the release PR itself runs no CI, because a `GITHUB_TOKEN`-authored PR starts no workflows) is filed and unassigned; it is not in the ruled set above.

### Also outstanding, unrelated to the ruling

The verification card's throwaway branch `claude/issue-5395-ci-cost-model-verification` could not be deleted — this session's proxy returns 403 for both `git push --delete` and the REST ref delete. It was emptied instead (`a07624e22`, empty diff against `main`); someone with delete rights should remove it.

⚠️ Two things a claiming seat should know, because this card is thin:
1. The body names no file and no measurement — it is a question, not a scoped card. The first deliverable is a measurement (where the time actually goes), and it is legitimate to come back with that and a re-scoped card rather than a fix.

Several already-routed `domain:devx` cards are plausible partial answers and should be read first rather than rediscovered: **#5410** (a gate passing `setParentNodes: true` for nothing — ~25% of two gates' dominant cost), **#5422** (`concurrency` cancelling the coverage job mid-run), **#5436** (coverage upload rejected), **#4986** (the merge queue that has never produced a build). If the measurement lands on one of those, close this as a duplicate rather than opening a parallel fix.

Re-grade (triage seat, session `session_01LsWeHbPzR3i6mmonFfGykk`, 2026-08-23 ~14:2xZ): `Blocked-by: #5395` resolved — the independent re-measurement was delivered and ACCEPTed (its report is the artifact; it corrected the cost model, e.g. release-lane median wait is 5m08s / 22% of wall clock, not ~35min). What remains on this card is not measurement but a ruling: the priced options cluster (2026-08-20T14:25Z comment) includes gate-shape changes — removing `pnpm test` from `changeset-release.yml` and altering concurrency-drop behavior are gate-weakening-class calls, which sit on the manual floor. `pm:blocked` → `needs-user-decision` in the same stroke. Note for the decision: option pieces already landed independently (coverage was 4-way sharded; `CODECOV_TOKEN` half resolved via #5436) — re-read the 14:25Z cluster against #5395's corrected numbers before ruling; the un-ruled residue is essentially option 3.

四维分析(补充,中文;选项与实测价格见卡上 2026-08-20T14:25Z 评论,此处不复述):
- **实际业务需求** — CI 时长直接吃每次合并的落地延迟;测量已证瓶颈与等待结构,修与不修都有明码标价。
- **项目长远合理性** — 分片与并发治理是可持续形态;从 release 工作流里删测试是用安全换速度,需要显式裁决而非顺手改。
- **防 AI 写代码犯错** — 门禁削弱类改动必须人裁:AI 有把 CI 弄绿的结构性动机,这正是人工地板存在的理由。
- **创业阶段不扩散需求** — 已落地的分片解决了大头;剩余选项只在维护者仍觉得慢时才值得做,不默认扩散。

推荐:若当前 CI 时长已可接受,关闭本卡(测量归档在 #5395);若仍要提速,先做并发丢跑治理(不削门禁),`changeset-release.yml` 删测试一项单独裁。

## Maintainer ruling recorded (atomic four-part write)

Ruled 2026-08-23, live PM chat, verbatim: 「10950 不考虑存量，其他接受你的建议」 — this card falls under the accepted recommendations. **Ruled: current CI duration is acceptable — closing.** The question is answered by the #5395 measurement (release-lane median wait 5m08s / 22% of wall, not ~35min; coverage now 4-way sharded; CODECOV half resolved via #5436). The un-ruled residue — removing `pnpm test` from `changeset-release.yml` (gate-weakening) — is NOT approved. If CI feels slow again, reopening is free: the first step then is concurrency-drop hygiene (95/200 runs never executed), which does not weaken any gate.
